# `aitbc wallet bridge sell lock`

Sign and submit the AIT lock to the escrow address. The TRANSFER is signed with THIS node's wallet key and submitted to the local chain RPC — the hub only ever sees the sealed transaction.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc wallet bridge sell lock [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--quote-id` | text | — | yes | Sell quote id from `sell quote`. |
| `--wallet-name` | text | — | no | Shop wallet name (signs the lock). |
| `--hub-url` | text | — | no | Hub wallet-service base URL — bare origin, path is stripped. |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc wallet bridge sell lock --quote-id <quote_id>
```
